content:
@Wrenna Robson, @François G. Dorais, batteries#1507 introduced some bad grind annotations, that have subsequently blown up in my face trying to fix something Mathlib.

Could I ask you both to exercise more care adding grind annotations? (I am guilty of the same!)

In particular,

@[grind _=_]
theorem findIdxNth_lt_length_iff {xs : List α} :
    xs.findIdxNth p n < xs.length ↔ n < xs.countP p := by
  induction xs generalizing n <;> grind

@[grind _=_]
theorem findIdxNth_eq_length_iff {xs : List α} :
    xs.findIdxNth p n = xs.length ↔ xs.countP p ≤ n := by
  induction xs generalizing n <;> grind

are not super helpful (maybe locally in the file? but start with local grind if that's all you want them for). In particular setting up ematching lemmas on inequality/equality patterns is rarely helpful, because there is no mechanism for grind to activate these just because its inequality module has proved these facts: it needs to see the literal inequality. (ematching is just not that tightly integrated with the inequality module)
I appreciate this is my fault for not writing a linter against these.
Thanks! Sorry about this - I am still slowly learning exactly what makes a good grind pattern.
batteries#1744 cleans up
Would really appreciate linters and that.
I have become a big convert to the church of Good Grind Lemmas but I'm aware they're not always hits.

More generally, could we try to be more careful to only add stuff to Batteries that is motivated by being needed in realistic downstream projects? Batteries is not a great place to practice paving wall-to-wall API, because the whole ecosystem suffers if you get it wrong.

Maybe we could even have a policy that stuff needs to go into a serious project first before it can be considered for PR'ing to Batteries.
I should say this work was motivated by some work I've been doing, it wasn't pie in the sky stuff.
Okay -- but the PR doesn't point to that, I think I would like to see that in batteries going forward: pointers to multi-contributor projects that need the material.
That's very fair - unfortunately that means I am a lot less likely to contribute because I don't necessarily immediately have collaborators.
Obviously this was not how Mario got this library started: but he was working before there were any libraries at all.
Mainly I just needed findIdxNth quite a bit, and the ensuing link between subpermutations and embeddings.
It seemed a useful and natural function without an inappropriate mathematical focus.

Sorry, I don't mean to be harsh. It's just that Batteries is expensive in terms of maintenance... Anything that goes wrong will blow up in my face when I'm keeping nightly-testing alive as Lean moves underneath it. It's nice to have test cases, but I'd prefer that they have more validation for "we should keep this working", e.g. it's important enough to get into Mathlib.
Indeed Mathlib is not really interested in such things in my experience.
Because they don't care about computable things.
So these things can just go in private libraries until there are users.
(I am working, soon, on some much more computable libraries! I feel your pain there. There's a lot we need to add. But it needs to be driven by big end goals, not API paving.)
In my experience that leads to a lot of duplication and wasted effort. I am not sure I know what you mean by API paving.
The goal here was: to try to extract from Mathlib (where this stuff exists in quite abstract terms) the notion that Perm/Subperm as predicates have a real and concrete meaning.
But what for?
There is an infinite space of "natural sounding" functions that could live in the List namespace.
Oh sure
(Sorry, have to run. Sorry if I've been critical here: I'm suffering a bit today from some serious new Lean features/breakages, and finding myself annoyed at every little hurdle I hit. :-)

My motivation originally is: I have spent quite a substantial amount of time (and have a large private repo which I created during my PhD) on concrete permutations as arrays, and in particular studying the algorithms to convert them to Benes networks a la Waksman.
This specifically has relevance to Classic McEliece (I can link you to a preprint I have in fact, though it's not really about the Lean content).
Okay! That's more like it. Let's have github.com/linesthatinterlace/Benes, and put the subperm stuff there. When someone else says "hey, I need that too", it's time for Batteries.
I do feel a little bit sensitive here to the implicit accusation that I'm just theorem proving to no end. I'm not.

It's just that to be quite frank discovery of these things is very poor. I'm aware of like four cases recently of people independently reinventing sorting networks (which are related to the permutation network construction).

Having seen what goes into CSLib and the priorities of that project, it's not clear to me that that is the home for this stuff, at least at present, and in any case I worry that building such things downstream of Mathlib encourages inappropriate amounts of importing large abstract theories that make it hard to use things elsewhere.
https://github.com/linesthatinterlace/controlbits exists, though I agree I could do more to structure it like a downstream library as opposed to a leaf project.

I find contributions to the lean ecosystem are constantly caught in this trap where you have to justify the motivation for something but you need the scaffolding to justify the motivation, and hence people simply don't bother - the labour is too high.
I thought I did the right thing here - I trusted FGD to tell me if this function wasn't appropriate for Batteries but it seemed to me to be the appropriate place.

I wouldn't dream of submitting such a thing to Core, but equally Mathlib is not the appropriate place for such things, especially nowadays when the preference is very clearly towards "mathematics in truth".
To be honest the Lean ecosystem often feels like quite a lonely and hostile place to build stuff.
I was both sick and busy for a while. Sorry for my late responses! :sad:
Oh we've only been talking for like 30 minutes!
I have found you very reasonable to work with for what it's worth.

It is a lot easier to contribute when it doesn't feel like suggestions and ideas are going to met with an immediate wall of "I don't know what that is and I don't understand why I should care and I don't trust that you have an expert perspective that might inform your thinking".
I prefer working carefully with people to build productive working relationships over time.

Oh! @Kim Morrison I forgot, but also the motivation of these functions was that it downstream will I think provide a chance to improve Multiset.ToType/is intimately linked to the relationship between List and Multiset - though that's more Mathlib-specific.
@Wrenna Robson, would you be able to get Mathlib working for batteries#1744? I would prefer not to get bogged down here, as I have many other repairs on nightly-testing I'm juggling.
Err it looked to me like it was failing for CI reasons rather than an actual error?
I have re-run the job. Again, I don't know that there is an error here because it failed pre-build as you will have seen.
I am seeing similar failures on unrelated PRs. I think the latest version of batteries may actually have Mathlib incompatibilities.
Which suggests someone merged a PR without checking for a mathlib break.
Yeah the issue existed on batteries#1736 certainly. I cannot get this working, or at least it is not limited to 1544.
